openings.claim: Current assignments may alter historical-week course membership; effective-date selection or explicit authorized week selection could restore it.
openings.discriminator: With attendance and identities fixed, does reassignment change the requested-week set?
openings.fit: Conditional: private center scope, documented CSV, concurrent attendance, six engineer-days and existing hosting.
openings.probe: Replay unchanged, midweek and postweek assignments against expected sets; test same-named courses across centers. If reproduced, estimate effective-date correction or explicit week selection.
openings.uncertainty: Selection dependency and recoverable history are unknown; explicit selection feasibility is also unproven. Otherwise remain diagnostic.

openings.claim: Renamed courses may be present but unrecognized against older timetables; a private rename mapping could reduce false omissions.
openings.discriminator: Complete renamed rows versus true missing rows; mapping must preserve omission detection.
openings.fit: Preserve private workspace, CSV and attendance access; implementation must share the six-day and hosting budget.
openings.probe: Six coordinators, two short sessions: counterbalance fabricated comparisons with/without mapping and an omitted-course control. Measure false alarms, missed omissions, checking, correction, download and import time.
openings.uncertainty: Recoverable identities, timetable accuracy and task realism remain unknown; mapping does not validate splits or isolation.

decision: Probe before choosing a change; correlation establishes no cause. Seven-minute stable-course handling limits universal-workflow claims; replacement waits exceed computation. Split-course isolation remains untested. Success requires next 40 exports: median handling <=12 minutes, >=95% intended sets, zero cross-center records.
